title: Inquest into death of Phonesay Chanthachack delayed
subtitle: An inquest into the death of Phonesay Chanthachack scheduled to begin Monday has been delayed until Tuesday.
article: An inquest into the death of Phonesay Chanthachack scheduled to begin Monday has been delayed until Tuesday.
Chanthachack was shot to death by Hamilton Police as they were trying to arrest him for failing to appear in court on a long list of theft-related charges.
Mandatory under the Coroners Act, the inquest was set to begin at 9:30 a.m. in the John Sopinka Courthouse, but was delayed for what were termed "procedural matters."

Initially the inquest was pushed back until 1:30 p.m. but it never formally convened and the court was adjourned for the day. Officials said the delay was to provide the parties time to review additional material.
Now scheduled to begin Tuesday at 9:30 a.m., the inquest is expected to last 10 days, and will hear from approximately 15 witnesses.
It will examine the events surrounding Chanthachack's death, and the jury may make recommendations aimed at preventing similar ones.
Dr. Jack Stanborough will preside as inquest coroner, and Graeme Leach will be counsel to the coroner.

Chanthachack, 27, nicknamed Pun, was facing 18 charges including break and enter, identity theft and credit card theft. When he failed to turn up in court on the morning of Feb 13, 2012, a warrant was issued for his arrest.
Not long after that, police encountered him in the area of Quigley and Albright roads, driving a stolen van.

According to the Special Investigations Unit (SIU) concluding report , Chanthachack was blocked in an Albright Road parking lot by police cruisers. (The province's Special Investigations Unit investigates all cases involving death or serious injury occurring during police action.)

The SIU said Chanthachack ignored commands to stop and attempted to drive away. He drove at Hamilton Constable Ryan Tocher, who fired two shots. The second, and fatal, shot passed through the window of the passenger side sliding door.
Tocher, who was clipped by the van after getting out of his vehicle to arrest Chanthachack, was cleared of any wrongdoing by the SIU last June.
